answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent network can deploy transitive trust graphs. Seed nodes serve as a trust anchor, propagating bounded scores along interaction edges. Adversaries incur the scarce cost of establishing organic, reciprocal links across topological bottlenecks, preventing bots from swooping like a raven to siphon tasks across ferrous server racks. However, honest newcomers suffer cold-start isolation, and clustered subgraphs can misclassify legitimate peers.
